title: A Unified Safety Subspace Exists in Speech Language Models
abstract: Speech Language Models (SLMs) extend large language models to spoken interaction, but this multimodal integration introduces modality-specific vulnerabilities. While prior work has typically addressed speech and text safety in isolation, our work uncovers a shared safety subspace where benign, harmful, and jailbreak representations exist regardless of input modality. We identify this subspace via a PCA projection, revealing a well-defined boundary separating refusal from jailbreak compliance. Causal intervention along this boundary shifts model behavior between refusal and compliance across modalities and attack types without additional training. For example, a refusal vector derived from an audio attack reduces text jailbreak success from 76.5% to 2.2%, while a refusal vector derived from the text attack reduces audio jailbreak success from 79.0% to 3.1%. We demonstrate these results on Qwen2-Audio and GLM-4-Voice, and confirm transferability across five different attacks.
relevance_note: Identifies a shared safety subspace across modalities in speech language models. User decision at review (2026-11-01): rejected as out of scope (interesting, but not about generating or evaluating synthetic speech).
